summary: OIDC 'aud' claim mismatch causing IAM-bound tokens to be rejected in Private deployment
description: Customer's private VPC deployment started seeing 401s for IAM-bound service tokens after a planned IdP configuration change. Tokens introspect as active at IdP but are rejected by Redwood's private control plane during token validation due to 'aud' mismatch. Issue began after customer updated application registration in their IdP (Okta) to support a new client alias.
impact: Multiple backend services in customer VPC could not authenticate: api calls to Redwood private control plane returned 401. This affected a production payments flow for Finnova, causing delayed settlements and customer-visible errors. Estimated affected traffic: ~12k requests/hour for 3 hours during peak retry window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use an OIDC-issued access token from Finnova's Okta tenant with 'aud' set to the Okta client alias 'finapps-v2'.
2) Send a request to the customer's private Redwood endpoint with Authorization: Bearer <token>.

3) Observe 401 response from private-control-plane. Token introspection at IdP returns active=true but the token's 'aud' claim does not match the audience configured in the control plane (expected 'redwood-private'), causing validation failure.
4) Update token 'aud' to 'redwood-private' (or add that audience in IdP) and retry — request is accepted.
logs: 2026-03-09T14:12:08Z auth-proxy ERROR token_validation.go:87 audience mismatch: token.aud=['finapps-v2'] expected=['redwood-private'] request_id=req-0a3f
2026-03-09T14:12:09Z control-plane WARN auth-validate token rejected code=401 reason=audience_mismatch user_agent=finapps-service
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: JWKS rotation or invalid signature — ruled out after verifying signature with jwks_uri and confirming kid present.
Observed that IdP token 'aud' value changed after customer re-registered client with an alias. Private control plane had strict single-audience matching configured (redwood-private).
Reproduced locally by minting token with aud 'finapps-v2' — validation returns audience_mismatch error in identity-proxy component.
Checked linked INT ticket INT-4021 where a similar audience-relaxation change was discussed for multi-tenant sync; decided not enabled in private by default for security reasons.
Customer provided Okta admin screen capture showing new client alias and a note that the change was intentional for internal routing.
Risk assessment: allowing multiple audiences increases attack surface if not tightly scoped. Temporary allowance should be narrowly scoped to the customer's client IDs and audited.
SRE verified no other customers impacted in hosted plane; scope was limited to customer private config in us-east.
Created a reproducer script and added to private-control-plane integration tests to prevent regression.
comments: Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-09: Customer reports all service-to-service calls started returning 401 after their IdP change at ~14:00 UTC. Asked for token sample and introspection output.

Fynn Morales (SRE) 2026-03-09: Confirmed audience mismatch in identity-proxy logs. No signature issues. Escalating to Eng for policy change. Slack: #support thread <https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234/support>.

Liam Chen (Eng) 2026-03-09: Working on a guarded config change that allows a configured list of acceptable audiences per-customer in private control plane. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/812.
Customer (FinNova Ops) 2026-03-09: We can revert the client alias but that will break another internal routing rule. Prefer allow-list approach on Redwood side.

Asha Patel 2026-03-10: Customer approved temporary allow-list entry. Applied change to their private control plane and monitored for 2 hours — traffic returned to normal. Planning follow-up to harden validation logic.
resolution: Implemented per-customer audience allow-list in the private control plane and deployed a targeted config change for Finnova. Verified successful authentication after adding 'finapps-v2' to the allowed audiences for their tenant. Reverted overly permissive test changes and added unit/integration tests to ensure only configured audiences are accepted. Communicated permanent guidance to customer: either include 'redwood-private' in their token audience or provide the exact client ID(s) to allow-list. Deployed patch to production us-east on 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC (rollout: canary -> 20% -> 100%).
follow_up_actions: 1) Update Private OIDC integration guide to document audience options and provide Okta steps for adding multiple audiences. Confluence page updated.
2) Add a validation error page in Console to show 'audience mismatch' with remediation steps for private customers.
3) Add automated test cases to CI for audience mismatch and allow-list behavior. PR referenced above merged and backported to release-2026-02.
4) Schedule a sync with Finnova on 2026-03-16 to review IdP configuration and finalize permanent audience plan.
5) Consider product decision on supporting multi-audience tokens by default for dedicated/private — add to roadmap discussion with Security and Product.
